items.video_description:
2018 Elantra Overheating

This is the second time visiting this 2018 Hyundai Elantra for an overheating issue. The first time was for a bypass tube/rubber hose junction leaking. This time, is for the same reason as last time. Slow loss of coolant allowing the engine to slowly build air cavataion and then overheating. At idle and around town it never really had any issues. When loaded down on the highway, however, the temperature stays high enough, to keep the cooling system under enough pressure to force coolant out in a VERY sneaky way. (Poor design)

"You've got no more excuses... Pick up those wrenches!"

items.video_title: Cracked Coolant Reservoir Symptoms, Repair And Cost
items.video_description:
Is your car leaking coolant or overheating? STOP DRIVING! A cracked coolant reservoir (expansion tank) is one of the most common—and most dangerous—cooling system failures. If left unchecked, this tiny plastic crack will boil your coolant, warp your cylinder heads, and cost you thousands in engine replacement!

We cover everything from safely diagnosing the hairline crack and checking for blown head gaskets, to a complete step-by-step replacement and the crucial "spill-free" bleeding procedure to get air out of your system.

⚠️ NEVER open your coolant system when the engine is hot! Scalding boiling fluid will erupt. Always wait for the engine to completely cool. Coolant is also highly toxic—clean up all spills immediately.

Chapters:
00:00 The Coolant Reservoir
01:04 Important Safety Warnings
02:00 Diagnosing a Cracked Reservoir
03:26 Tools and Materials Needed

06:49 Step 3: Installing the New Reservoir
07:38 Step 4: Refilling & Bleeding the System
08:42 Cracked Coolant Reservoir Repair Costs
10:19 Post-Repair Verification & Testing
